x: In a repeat clash of the three leading British Juniors, Richard Dorman beat his personal best,but in a close race was beaten into third place. 1.G.Vale (S.W.C.) 12.42; 2.I.McCombie (North Shields) 12.49; 3.R.Dorman 12.51.
After a lap of the Park in the lead was Ian McCombie with Paul Blagg just behind, packing in was Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton and a battle for 4th place between John's Newnham and Hall.
Another multi-lap course gave Ian McCombie a superb time of 86.21 and selection for the European, but no Belgrave man in the frame. 1.I.McCombie (Camb.H.) 86.21. 7.J.Hall 96.49. 9.C.Lawton 101.51.

The weather turned to spring and the sun shone on Belgrave.In the Southern 10 won by Ian McCombie,Richard Dorman came through for 3rd and with backing from Lawton,Warburton and Scamell team victory was ours.
Ian McCombie dominated the race from the start and eit was left to Murray Day to come home a distant 2nd. Belgrave backed well to finish 4 in 9 and an easy win.

Cold damp miserable, best described London's Thamesmead, but despite that produced a British best by Ian McCombie. Belgrave could not touch Leicester with 4 in 10 but almost beat Coventry despite uncertainty as to who would score.
On the multi-lap course around the chocolate factory with the wind blowing across the race course it was Ian McCombie who retained his title without much effort.
